message.content:
Paris is home to many iconic landmarks, but if you’re looking for the single most famous place, it’s almost certainly **the Eiffel Tower**. Here’s why it stands out and a quick rundown of other must-see spots:

| # | Place | Why It’s Famous | Quick Facts |
|---|-------|-----------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Eiffel Tower** | Symbol of Paris, engineering marvel, romantic views | Built 1889, 324 m tall, 1.5 million visitors/year |
| 2 | **Louvre Museum** | Largest art museum, Mona Lisa | 35 000 artworks, 9 million visitors/year |
| 3 | **Notre-Dame Cathedral** | Gothic architecture, historic significance | 12th‑century masterpiece (rebuilding after 2019 fire) |
| 4 | **Champs‑Élysées & Arc de Triomphe** | Iconic avenue, national monument | 1.5 km long, 8 million visitors/year |
| 5 | **Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur** | Bohemian history, panoramic city view | 19th‑century hilltop church |
| 6 | **Palace of Versailles** | Royal opulence, Hall of Mirrors | 17th‑century palace, 10 million visitors/year |
| 7 | **Sainte‑Chapelle** | Stunning stained‑glass windows | 13th‑century chapel |
| 8 | **Luxembourg Gardens** | Beautiful gardens, French formal style | 25 ha park, 5 million visitors/year |
| 9 | **Centre Pompidou** | Modern art museum, architectural icon | 20th‑century modern art collection |
|10 | **Père Lachaise Cemetery** | Famous graves, cultural heritage | 1.5 ha cemetery, 1 million visitors/year |

### Quick Tips for Visiting
- **Eiffel Tower**: Book tickets online to skip the line; consider visiting at sunset for stunning light shows.
- **Louvre**: Arrive early or late to avoid crowds; use the “Louvre Pass” for free entry to other museums.
- **Notre-Dame**: Check restoration updates; the interior is still closed to visitors as of 2024.
- **Versailles**: Allocate a full day; the gardens and palace are both worth exploring.

Enjoy your trip to Paris!
